Trans-Cinnamaldehyde is a component of cinnamon spice and a principal constituent of the European Standard 'Fragrance Mix' used in patch testing. It acts as a skin sensitiser in humans, with differing potencies (Johansen et al., 1996a,b).
α-Alkyl substituted cinnamaldehydes (e.g. methyl-, butyl-, amyl- and hexyl-cinnamaldehyde) are used in the fragrance industry and all act as skin sensitisers in humans (Johansen et al., 1996a,b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.05-0.5% cinnamaldehyde in base cream or 99% ethanol, closed patch test, applied to back/forearm/upper arm for 24-48 h, read 30 min after removal
evidence.support_text: Closed patch tests were conducted on 155 patients with 0.05–0.5% cinnamaldehyde in a base cream or in 99% ethanol. Patches consisted of a piece of 1 cm² lint with a 2 cm² cellophane disc placed on the lint and then covered with a 4 cm² plaster. The patches were applied to the back, the forearm and the inside of the upper arm for 24–48 h. Reactions were read 30 min after patch removal. Erythema was observed in 3 patients (Takekawa et al., 1986).
